### (a) Who controls the source?

The source is `chrome.runtime.onMessageExternal.addListener(...)` at `gen/ext_bg_module.js:122`. The listener dispatches on the attacker/peer-supplied `req.cmd` and `req.url` fields with **no sender validation**.

The manifest's `externally_connectable.matches` is:

```
["https://*.crankwheel.com/*", "https://*.meeting.is/*"]
```
No `ids` are declared, so the reachable senders are web pages on those origins (and any subdomain), not other extensions. An ordinary user cannot post this from `evil.com`, but:
- any page on `crankwheel.com` / `meeting.is` (or any subdomain) can send it, and
- an XSS/subdomain-takeover on those trusted origins is a bypassable precondition.

Per the audit rules, this is a web-origin external-message surface (exploitable via XSS), **not** a browser-authenticated extension-ID boundary.
